findings.title: Cleanup job ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The background cleanup loop's ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This makes every cleanup job (temp file scans, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) run 10x more often on every Grafana instance, which is a significant and unrelated increase in DB and filesystem load for a PR whose purpose is to avoid annotation deadlocks. Given the per-run timeout is still 9 minutes, this looks like leftover debugging to make the annotation cleanup fire quickly during testing and should be reverted to 10 minutes.

findings.title: Leftover debug logging emitted at Error level on every cleanup batch
findings.body: `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", ...)` (and the equivalent calls at lines 537, 554, 557, 576, 579) log normal, successful operation at Error severity. Every cleanup cycle will therefore emit error-level log lines even when nothing is wrong, which pollutes logs and triggers error-based alerting/monitoring for operators. In addition, these lines dump the full `ids` slice, which can be tens of thousands of integers per batch (the new test uses a batch size of 32767), producing very large log records. These should be removed or demoted to Debug without the full ID list.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when inlining IDs for SQLite
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, the SQLite fallback builds the `IN (...)` list with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside a loop, re-allocating and copying the whole accumulated string on each iteration. With the batch sizes this code path is designed for (the new test exercises 32767 IDs per batch), this is O(n^2) in allocations and bytes copied and runs for every batch of every cleanup cycle. Use `strings.Builder` (or `strconv.AppendInt` into a byte slice, as done in `getAccessControlFilter`) instead.

findings.title: Parameterized delete can exceed placeholder limits on non-SQLite databases
findings.body: The parameter-limit workaround in `deleteByIDs` is gated on `r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite`. For other backends the code always emits one `?` placeholder per ID. PostgreSQL has a hard limit of 65535 bind parameters per statement, so an operator who sets `annotation_cleanup_job_batch_size` above that value will get a driver error on every cleanup batch and annotation cleanup will stop working, with no indication that the batch size is the cause. Either cap the number of IDs per DELETE statement (chunking) regardless of backend, or base the inline-values decision on `len(ids)` against a per-dialect limit.

findings.title: Table cleanup registered after assertions that can abort the subtest
findings.body: `t.Cleanup` that truncates `annotation`/`annotation_tag` is registered only after `createTestAnnotations` and the two `assertAnnotationCount`/`assertAnnotationTagCount` calls, which use `require` and abort the subtest on failure. If any of those assertions fail, the rows inserted by this subtest are never deleted, and because `fakeSQL` is shared across all subtests in the table the subsequent cases will see leftover rows and fail with confusing counts, masking the original failure. Register the cleanup immediately after obtaining the session / before inserting the test data.

findings.title: Comment states an outdated SQLite parameter limit inconsistent with the new test
findings.body: The comment says "SQLite has a parameter limit of 999" and the constant is `sqliteParameterLimit = 999`, while the new test case is named "should not fail if batch size is larger than SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER for SQLite >= 3.32.0" (which is 32766). The two descriptions disagree about what limit is being guarded against; a reader cannot tell whether 999 is intentionally conservative (pre-3.32 builds) or simply wrong. Clarify the comment to state that 999 is the pre-3.32.0 limit and is used conservatively.
